title: Excess of a Post-Death Deposit on Joint and Period-Certain Income Annuities
content:
The excess of a deposit made on an Ashgrove Income Annuities contract after a death — the part that was not owed to the person paid — is fixed for two kinds of tier:

1. **Joint-and-survivor tier, contract continuing to the survivor.** On a joint-and-survivor tier (Joint 50% Survivor or Joint 100% Survivor) whose contract status is survivor continuing, the excess of a deposit whose payment date fell after the first death is the deposit less the survivor's entitlement for that payment date.
2. **Period-certain tier.** On a period-certain tier (10-Year Certain or 20-Year Certain), a deposit falling due on or before the certain period end date has no excess, being owed to the beneficiary.

For any other deposit neither rule applies.

The first death date and the certain period end date are those recorded on the contract; the deposit's payment date is the one on its activity entry.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Tier and status | Deposit's payment date | Excess |
|---|---|---|
| Joint 50% Survivor, survivor continuing; first death 10 May | 1 June | Deposit less the survivor's entitlement for 1 June |
| Joint 50% Survivor, survivor continuing; first death 1 June | 1 June (the death date itself, not after it) | Neither rule applies |
| Joint 100% Survivor, death claim pending; first death 10 May | 1 June | Neither rule applies (not survivor continuing) |
| 20-Year Certain; certain period ends 1 September | 1 September | None, owed to the beneficiary |
| 20-Year Certain; certain period ends 1 September | 1 October | Neither rule applies |
